sections: Deployment mode (drives DB and document storage selection)

variables.description: Development | staging | production
variables.label: Application environment

variables.description: True locally, ALWAYS false in production
variables.label: Debug mode

variables.description: Comma-separated exact browser origins. Empty disables cross-origin access, and empty is the supported configuration: one container serves the interface and /api on one origin, so nothing is cross-origin. Each entry must read exactly as a browser sends it -- no trailing slash, no path, and no default port (https://app.example.com, never https://app.example.com:443).
variables.label: Allowed browser origins

variables.description: Names the Compose project and, with it, the lumina-data volume. Changing it on an existing deployment points Lumina at an empty volume.
variables.label: Compose project name

variables.description: The image Compose pulls. Unset means ghcr.io/coddesigning/lumina:latest, built from main. A full commit SHA in place of latest pins one release.
variables.label: Container image

variables.description: The single published port: one container serves the interface and /api together, so this is the whole address. After startup Lumina is at http://127.0.0.1:10312. Change it here alone -- nothing needs rebuilding, because the interface calls /api on whatever origin served it.
variables.label: Published port

variables.description: Published on every interface by default, so other devices on your network can reach Lumina immediately. Set 127.0.0.1 to keep it on this machine only, or a specific address (e.g. a Tailscale address) to limit it to that network. Restrict /health/* at the edge if this machine is exposed beyond a trusted network.
variables.label: Bind address

variables.description: Addresses whose X-Forwarded-For the API believes. Unset by default, and that is the safe value: nothing sits between a browser and the container, so no forwarded address is trusted and per-IP rate limits key on the real peer. Set this ONLY to the address of a TLS reverse proxy you run yourself. Any wider value lets a caller send its own X-Forwarded-For and so choose its own rate-limit identity, which defeats the login and registration limits below.
variables.label: Forwarded allow IPs

variables.description: Where the built interface lives. The image sets this to the build output it baked in; leave it unset outside a container to serve the API alone.
variables.label: Web root

variables.description: Must hold two spooled copies of each concurrent maximum-size upload, plus overhead.
variables.label: Container /tmp size

variables.description: Ceilings each container runs under. Compose applies these to a plain `docker compose up` as well, not only under Swarm. The API and the worker share these two: embedding and OCR are the memory-hungry step, so a host with less to spare lowers them together.
variables.label: CPU limit

variables.description: Memory ceiling for each container, in Docker units such as 4G or 512M. Extraction and embedding are the hungry stages.
variables.label: Memory limit

variables.description: docker-compose.hosted.yml only, for the database and object store it runs beside the application. The self-hosted stack has neither.
variables.label: Postgres CPU limit

variables.description: Memory ceiling for that PostgreSQL container.
variables.label: Postgres memory limit

variables.description: CPU ceiling for the MinIO container in the hosted topology.
variables.label: Minio CPU limit

variables.description: Memory ceiling for that MinIO container.
variables.label: Minio memory limit

variables.description: Host directory for encrypted/off-host backup handling; never place it in the lumina-data volume. Override the archive name for every scheduled backup.
variables.label: Lumina backup directory

variables.description: File name given to the archive inside LUMINA_BACKUP_DIRECTORY. Give each scheduled run its own name or the previous archive is overwritten.
variables.label: Backup archive name

variables.description: Compose .env values containing $ must be single-quoted to prevent interpolation. Required in production and hosted mode. Development may use an ephemeral key.
variables.label: JWT secret key

variables.description: Optional dedicated secret for encrypting user-provided BYOK API keys at rest. When unset, the encryption key is securely derived from JWT_SECRET_KEY.
variables.label: Encryption key

variables.description: Optional when self-hosted: leave both empty and the first account to register becomes the administrator. Set both to reserve that account for one address, which then registers once with the token as X-Bootstrap-Token. Hosted mode requires both. Prefer a generated URL-safe token without $.
variables.label: Bootstrap admin email

variables.description: Proof required from the reserved address when it registers, sent as the X-Bootstrap-Token header. At least 32 visible ASCII characters.
variables.label: Bootstrap admin token

variables.description: SYSTEM_SETTINGS_DIRECTORY holds the administrator-managed configuration overrides, the last-known-good revision and the restart request state. It must be on durable storage, so the container pins it to /data/system-settings. It is never itself overridable: the override store cannot be moved by an override it would have to read from the new location to find.
variables.label: Override store directory

variables.description: Whether a supervisor restarts this process after it exits. The container image sets it true because Compose declares restart: unless-stopped. Where it is false, Lumina refuses the in-product restart instead of exiting into nothing.
variables.label: Supervised restart

variables.description: How long a requested restart waits for in-flight document and generation jobs to finish before it proceeds, 0-3600. Work still running at the deadline is returned to the queue without spending an attempt, so nothing is lost.
variables.label: Restart drain timeout

variables.section: Deployment mode (drives DB and document storage selection)
variables.description: self_hosted -> SQLite + local filesystem document storage hosted -> PostgreSQL + S3-compatible storage; production requires s3
variables.label: Deployment mode

variables.description: Production self_hosted SQLite must use an absolute path with an existing parent. self_hosted development example: sqlite:///./data/lumina.db hosted example: postgresql+psycopg://USER:PASSWORD@HOST:5432/lumina
variables.label: Database URL

variables.description: Hosted PostgreSQL runtime pool. With RDS Proxy these values bound each API/worker process; total possible clients are replicas * (size + overflow).
variables.label: Database pool size

variables.description: Extra connections a process may open beyond the pool when it is saturated, 0-20. Pool plus overflow is the per-process ceiling.
variables.label: Database max overflow

variables.description: Seconds before an idle pooled connection is discarded and reopened, 60-3600. Keep it under any proxy or database idle timeout.
variables.label: Database pool recycle seconds

variables.description: Self-hosted API and worker processes append sanitized operational events to this dedicated SQLite file. The container overrides it to the shared /data volume. Hosted deployments ignore the path and read the fixed CloudWatch log group configured by infrastructure instead.
variables.label: Operational log path

variables.description: Compose overrides this to true. Leave false for an ordinary development checkout unless durable local diagnostics are deliberately wanted.
variables.label: Operational log persistence enabled

variables.description: Days an operational event is kept before the background trim deletes it, 1-366.
variables.label: Operational log retention days

variables.description: Hard ceiling on stored events, 10000-10000000. The oldest rows are trimmed first, so this bounds the file even if retention has not elapsed.
variables.label: Operational log max records

variables.description: Budget for one administrator log query, 1-30. A heavy filter is refused rather than allowed to hold the database open.
variables.label: Operational log query timeout seconds

variables.description: Hosted only. Never accept a log group from an API request.
variables.label: CloudWatch log group

variables.description: AWS region that log group lives in. Hosted only.
variables.label: CloudWatch region

variables.description: VECTOR_BACKEND selects where chunk embeddings live. It defaults to the backend that matches DATABASE_URL: pgvector on PostgreSQL, chroma on SQLite. Setting pgvector with a non-PostgreSQL DATABASE_URL fails at startup. CHROMA_PERSIST_DIRECTORY holds the self-hosted vector collection and must be on durable storage; losing it means re-running the embedding backfill. CHROMA_PERSIST_DIRECTORY and UPLOAD_DIRECTORY must be absolute when the local backend or chroma vectors are used in production; hosted + s3 ignores both. Provision the production UPLOAD_DIRECTORY before application startup.
variables.label: Vector backend

variables.description: Where the self-hosted Chroma collection is written. Must be durable storage: losing it means re-running the embedding backfill.
variables.label: Chroma persist directory

variables.description: RETRIEVAL_CHUNK_LIMIT is how many of a course's chunks semantic retrieval ranks for one generation request. RETRIEVAL_MIN_SIMILARITY is the cosine floor (0.0-1.0) below which a ranked chunk is discarded; when nothing clears the floor the request is rejected without calling the AI provider. Set the floor to 0.0 to disable it.
variables.label: Retrieval chunk limit

variables.description: Cosine floor a ranked chunk must clear, 0.0-1.0. Nothing above the floor means the request is refused rather than answered from weak material. Set 0.0 to disable.
variables.label: Retrieval min similarity

variables.description: STORAGE_BACKEND selects where uploaded documents live: local -> filesystem under UPLOAD_DIRECTORY (self-hosted) s3 -> S3-compatible bucket; hosted production requires s3
variables.label: Storage backend

variables.description: Prefix every stored object key carries, 1-40 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -. Changing it orphans existing documents; they are not moved.
variables.label: Storage namespace

variables.description: Where uploaded documents are written under the local storage backend. Must be durable storage and absolute in production.
variables.label: Upload directory

variables.description: S3_BUCKET must exist; the hosted Compose creates it via minio-init. Without S3_ENDPOINT_URL (real AWS), S3_REGION is required. Static credentials are optional on AWS (prefer IAM roles); MinIO requires both keys.
variables.label: S3 bucket

variables.description: Bucket region. Required when no endpoint URL is set, which is the real-AWS case.
variables.label: S3 region

variables.description: Address of an S3-compatible service such as MinIO. Leave it unset for real AWS.
variables.label: S3 endpoint URL

variables.description: Static access key. Optional on AWS, where an IAM role is preferred; MinIO requires it. Set both keys or neither.
variables.label: S3 access key ID

variables.description: Secret paired with that access key. Single-quote it if it contains $.
variables.label: S3 secret access key

variables.description: Whether to address buckets as a path rather than a subdomain. MinIO needs true; real AWS does not.
variables.label: S3 force path style

variables.description: Largest document a student may upload. Enforced before the body is read, so an oversized file is refused rather than buffered.
variables.label: Max upload size bytes

variables.description: Ceiling on an ordinary JSON request body. Uploads are bounded separately by MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_BYTES.
variables.label: Max request size bytes

variables.description: How many uploads may be validated at once before the rest wait. Validation reads bytes, so this bounds memory during a burst.
variables.label: Max concurrent document validations

variables.description: Pages of one PDF processed in parallel inside a single extraction. Multiplies with PROCESSING_JOB_CONCURRENCY for total CPU processes.
variables.label: PDF page workers

variables.description: Total deadline for upload admission and body receipt.
variables.label: Upload request timeout seconds

variables.description: How many documents one course may hold.
variables.label: Max documents per course

variables.description: Total stored bytes one course may hold across all of its documents.
variables.label: Max course storage bytes

variables.description: Pages a single PDF may contain before it is refused, so one enormous file cannot occupy a worker slot indefinitely.
variables.label: Max PDF pages

variables.description: Pixel ceiling for one rendered PDF page. A decompression bomb is refused here rather than during rasterisation.
variables.label: Max PDF page pixels

variables.description: Pixel ceiling summed across every page of one PDF.
variables.label: Max PDF total pixels

variables.description: Ceiling on a single decompressed PDF content stream, which is the other half of the decompression-bomb guard.
variables.label: Max PDF content stream bytes

variables.description: Drawing operations one PDF page may issue. A page that exceeds it is pathological rather than large.
variables.label: Max PDF drawing operations

variables.description: Embeddings are computed in this process by fastembed (ONNX, CPU) and are completely independent of which vendor answers a generation request: the same vectors are produced whether this deployment talks to Gemini, to Ollama, or to nothing. Ollama is therefore no longer required for a document to become ready. There is no model setting: the model is pinned in backend/app/embedding_models.py because the stored vector width, its CHECK constraints and its HNSW indexes are built for exactly that model, so changing it is an Alembic revision rather than an environment edit. Only where the ONNX weights live varies. Container images bake them at build time and never reach the network at runtime; a checkout downloads them once with `python scripts/fetch_embedding_model.py`.
variables.label: Embedding model cache directory

variables.description: Texts per forward pass, 1-256.
variables.label: Embedding batch size

variables.description: There is no image provider setting. Descriptions of diagrams, tables and charts are extracted once by the background worker and stored on the document, where every reader of that course shares them, so this can never be a per-user choice. The deployment uses the first vision-capable model of the first available vendor that has an image implementation (gemini or ollama); with none, visual extraction is skipped and recorded as not_configured. Describing a visual is a paid call per image, so a deployment can decline it without giving up the vendor that would otherwise answer.
variables.label: Image understanding enabled

variables.description: Budget for describing one visual, 1-300. Exceeding it records that visual as failed without failing the document.
variables.label: Image understanding timeout seconds

variables.description: Largest visual sent to the model, 1KiB-50MiB. Anything bigger is skipped rather than resized.
variables.label: Image understanding max bytes

variables.description: How many visuals an extraction attempt describes before deferring the rest to the background describe_visuals job. Describing one visual costs tens of seconds, so this must stay small relative to PROCESSING_JOB_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: a document whose visuals all had to be described inline could never finish within one attempt.
variables.label: Image understanding inline max visuals

variables.description: How long a claimed document job stays leased to one worker slot, 5-86400. Once it expires another slot may recover the job, so this bounds how long a killed worker can strand work.
variables.label: Processing job lease seconds

variables.description: Attempts a document job gets before it is recorded as failed, 1-100. A shutdown that returns a job to the queue does not spend an attempt.
variables.label: Processing job max attempts

variables.description: Seconds a worker slot waits between polls while the document queue is empty.
variables.label: Processing job poll seconds

variables.description: Wall-clock budget for one document extraction attempt, 1-86400. An attempt that exceeds it is abandoned and retried while attempts remain.
variables.label: Processing job attempt timeout seconds

variables.description: Documents processed at once by one worker process. Each slot needs two database connections, so hosted deployments must keep 2 * PROCESSING_JOB_CONCURRENCY + 1 within DATABASE_POOL_SIZE plus DATABASE_MAX_OVERFLOW. Maximum 6.
variables.label: Processing job concurrency

variables.description: Course and profile uploads share this per-account active-job ceiling. It counts extraction jobs only: a background describe_visuals job runs for minutes to hours and must not keep its owner from uploading.
variables.label: Processing job max active per user

variables.description: Visual description runs as its own job after a document is ready, and its progress is checkpointed per visual, so one long attempt is cheaper than many short ones: every retry re-pays the PDF parse, OCR and chunking that the attempt also performs.
variables.label: Describe visuals attempt timeout seconds

variables.description: Visual-description jobs one account may have running at once, 1-10. Counted separately from extraction so a long description cannot block an upload.
variables.label: Describe visuals max active per user

variables.description: How often the worker looks for ready documents still carrying a visual that nothing described, including documents processed while visual analysis was switched off. Each document is queued once. Set to 0 to disable the sweep.
variables.label: Visual description sweep interval seconds

variables.description: Durable AI generation uses separate slots in the same worker process. A student's third active request remains queued until one of the first two ends.
variables.label: Generation job lease seconds

variables.description: Attempts a backgrounded generation gets before it is recorded as failed, 1-100.
variables.label: Generation job max attempts

variables.description: Seconds a worker slot waits between polls while the generation queue is empty.
variables.label: Generation job poll seconds

variables.description: Wall-clock budget for one backgrounded generation attempt, 1-86400.
variables.label: Generation job attempt timeout seconds

variables.description: Generation claim slots inside one worker process, 1-6. Each slot costs a job connection plus a heartbeat connection from the database pool.
variables.label: Generation job concurrency

variables.description: Backgrounded generations one account may have running at once, 1-10.
variables.label: Generation job max active per user

variables.description: Stop grace per mode: abort needs 60s; drain the largest attempt timeout + 45s.
variables.label: Worker shutdown mode

variables.description: How long Compose waits for the worker to stop before killing it. Read by Compose, not the application: abort needs about 60s, drain needs the largest attempt timeout plus 45s.
variables.label: Worker stop grace period

variables.description: Characters kept from one document. Text past the ceiling is dropped, so a single enormous file cannot fill the database.
variables.label: Max extracted characters

variables.description: Chunks one document may produce. Each chunk costs one stored embedding.
variables.label: Max document chunks

variables.description: Tesseract language packs to load, plus-joined such as eng+tur. Only packs installed in the image can be named; the image ships eng.
variables.label: OCR language

variables.description: Resolution a page is rasterised at before OCR. Higher reads small type better and costs proportionally more time and memory.
variables.label: OCR resolution (DPI)

variables.description: Characters a page must already contain to be treated as digital text. Below it the page is treated as a scan and sent to OCR.
variables.label: OCR min text characters

variables.description: Target size of one retrievable chunk. It bounds how much context a single retrieval hit can carry.
variables.label: Document chunk size characters

variables.description: Characters repeated between neighbouring chunks so a sentence split across the boundary is still retrievable. Must be below the chunk size.
variables.label: Document chunk overlap characters

variables.description: Automatic background cleanup and vector synchronization. Set an interval to 0 to disable that maintenance cycle in the background worker. COURSE_PURGE_INTERVAL_SECONDS: seconds between scans for stranded tombstoned courses.
variables.label: Course purge interval seconds

variables.description: COURSE_PURGE_OPERATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: PostgreSQL lock/statement timeout budget given to the delete of one course (vectors, documents, chunks, quizzes). Widens the shared engine's default 5s cap so a large course's purge is not aborted mid-transaction by QueryCanceled.
variables.label: Course purge operation timeout seconds

variables.description: EMBEDDING_BACKFILL_INTERVAL_SECONDS: seconds between scans for missing vectors.
variables.label: Embedding backfill interval seconds

variables.description: Chunks the backfill embeds per pass. Larger batches finish sooner and hold more memory while they run.
variables.label: Embedding backfill batch size

variables.description: Whether the backfill also deletes vectors whose chunk no longer exists.
variables.label: Embedding backfill prune orphans

variables.description: AI_USAGE_RETENTION_DAYS: masked AI-usage telemetry older than this is deleted by the background worker on the interval below. AI_USAGE_CLEANUP_INTERVAL_SECONDS is the seconds between those retention scans; set it to 0 to disable the cycle (a one-off `python -m workers.ai_usage_cleanup` still works).
variables.label: AI usage retention days

variables.description: Telemetry rows deleted per pass, so a long retention change cannot hold one long transaction open.
variables.label: AI usage cleanup batch size

variables.description: Seconds between retention scans; 0 disables the cycle and leaves `python -m workers.ai_usage_cleanup` as the manual path.
variables.label: AI usage cleanup interval seconds

variables.description: Maximum characters of course material placed into one generation request, per feature. Each value must be at least DOCUMENT_CHUNK_SIZE_CHARACTERS. Study guide, quiz, AI tutor, course Q&A, and exam analysis head each retrieved passage with a citation key, which spends part of the budget, so they carry a wider one than flashcards, which emit no citations. See docs/citations.md. MATERIAL_MAX_CHARS_CEILING caps every per-feature budget below to this many characters when set (must also be >= DOCUMENT_CHUNK_SIZE_CHARACTERS). Set it once for a small local context window instead of lowering each budget.
variables.label: Material max chars ceiling

variables.description: Character budget for study guide generation. At least DOCUMENT_CHUNK_SIZE_CHARACTERS, and clamped by MATERIAL_MAX_CHARS_CEILING.
variables.label: Study guide material max chars

variables.description: Character budget for quiz generation. At least DOCUMENT_CHUNK_SIZE_CHARACTERS, and clamped by MATERIAL_MAX_CHARS_CEILING.
variables.label: Quiz material max chars

variables.description: Character budget for flashcard generation. At least DOCUMENT_CHUNK_SIZE_CHARACTERS, and clamped by MATERIAL_MAX_CHARS_CEILING.
variables.label: Flashcard material max chars

variables.description: Character budget for the AI tutor. At least DOCUMENT_CHUNK_SIZE_CHARACTERS, and clamped by MATERIAL_MAX_CHARS_CEILING.
variables.label: AI tutor material max chars

variables.description: Character budget for course Q&A. At least DOCUMENT_CHUNK_SIZE_CHARACTERS, and clamped by MATERIAL_MAX_CHARS_CEILING.
variables.label: Course Q&A material max chars

variables.description: Character budget for exam source analysis. At least DOCUMENT_CHUNK_SIZE_CHARACTERS, and clamped by MATERIAL_MAX_CHARS_CEILING.
variables.label: Exam analysis material max chars

variables.description: Character budget for reading a past paper. At least DOCUMENT_CHUNK_SIZE_CHARACTERS, and clamped by MATERIAL_MAX_CHARS_CEILING.
variables.label: Exam past paper max chars

variables.description: Character budget for an exam topic guide. At least DOCUMENT_CHUNK_SIZE_CHARACTERS, and clamped by MATERIAL_MAX_CHARS_CEILING.
variables.label: Exam topic guide material max chars

variables.description: Character budget for an exam topic summary. At least DOCUMENT_CHUNK_SIZE_CHARACTERS, and clamped by MATERIAL_MAX_CHARS_CEILING.
variables.label: Exam topic summary material max chars

variables.description: Character budget for an exam topic quiz. At least DOCUMENT_CHUNK_SIZE_CHARACTERS, and clamped by MATERIAL_MAX_CHARS_CEILING.
variables.label: Exam topic quiz material max chars

variables.description: Character budget for similar-question generation. At least DOCUMENT_CHUNK_SIZE_CHARACTERS, and clamped by MATERIAL_MAX_CHARS_CEILING.
variables.label: Exam similar questions material max chars

variables.description: Character budget for mock exam generation. At least DOCUMENT_CHUNK_SIZE_CHARACTERS, and clamped by MATERIAL_MAX_CHARS_CEILING.
variables.label: Exam mock exam material max chars

variables.description: Character budget for the exam review sheet. At least DOCUMENT_CHUNK_SIZE_CHARACTERS, and clamped by MATERIAL_MAX_CHARS_CEILING.
variables.label: Exam review sheet material max chars

variables.description: Questions in a generated mock exam, 1-20. Allocation reserves one question per requested topic, so a paper too short to cover them all is refused.
variables.label: Exam mock exam question count

variables.description: Questions in a practice quiz or topic exam when the student names no count, 1-20.
variables.label: Exam quiz default question count

variables.description: A vendor is available because its credential or endpoint is configured, and for no other reason. There is no provider selector: set a key and its models appear in GET /api/models; unset it and they are gone. GEMINI_API_KEY -> gemini:* models OPENAI_API_KEY -> openai:* models ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -> claude:* models OLLAMA_BASE_URL -> ollama:* models Startup fails if this leaves no model at all. A placeholder is not a comment here: any non-blank value advertises that vendor, so leave a key empty rather than filling in an example. See docs/ai_providers.md. There is no fallback setting either. Every available vendor joins the chain, the selected model's vendor first and the rest in the fixed order ollama, gemini, openai, claude. Configuring a paid key therefore accepts that an outage of one vendor bills the next one; GET /api/admin/ai-costs reports the spend per vendor and model. Optional deployment default, an exact provider:model id from GET /api/models. Unset, it is the first model of the first available vendor in that same fixed order - local first, because a local model costs nothing and sends no course material anywhere. A user's preferred_model overrides it; a request's explicit model overrides both.
variables.label: Default AI model

variables.description: Optional JSON model catalog keyed by provider. When set it is authoritative: a vendor whose credential is configured but which the catalog does not list is a startup error rather than a silent omission.
variables.label: AI model catalog

variables.description: Per-million-token prices used to estimate spend, as the JSON object shown above. Empty means generations are recorded without a cost estimate.
variables.label: AI model cost rates

variables.description: Per-request deadline for one generation, every provider. Raise it for local models on modest hardware; they are far slower than a hosted API.
variables.label: AI generation timeout seconds

variables.description: Attempts one provider call gets before the chain moves to the next vendor, 1-10.
variables.label: AI generation max attempts

variables.description: First wait between provider retries. It doubles each attempt up to the maximum below.
variables.label: AI generation backoff base seconds

variables.description: Ceiling on that doubling wait. Must be at least the base.
variables.label: AI generation backoff max seconds

variables.description: Provider calls in flight at once across the process, 1-100. It is the main guard against a vendor rate limit.
variables.label: AI generation max concurrency

variables.description: Self-hosted Ollama. The model must already be pulled on that instance and must reliably emit JSON; docs/ai_providers.md lists the capability bar. Ollama has no default any more, because a default would mean every deployment always claims a local server. Setting this is what makes ollama:* models appear. Root Compose reaches an Ollama process on the host through this name; use http://localhost:11434 when running Python directly. On Linux, start Ollama with OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434 and firewall the port to the Docker bridge.
variables.label: Ollama base URL

variables.description: One model answers both text generation and image understanding, so it must be multimodal for visual analysis to work. A text-only model is declared through AI_MODEL_CATALOG with "vision": false, which switches visual analysis off truthfully instead of sending it images it cannot read.
variables.label: Ollama model

variables.description: Sampling options sent with every Ollama request. Ollama's own defaults are tuned for chat, not for schema-constrained JSON; temperature 0.8 makes a small model violate hard constraints such as "exactly four options" often enough to fail whole generations. See the single-GPU box profile in docs/ai_providers.md.
variables.label: Ollama temperature

variables.description: Nucleus sampling cutoff, 0.01-1.0. Lower keeps the model to its most likely tokens.
variables.label: Ollama top p

variables.description: num_ctx is sent per request, so the model does not need a custom Modelfile and a server-wide OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH cannot silently inflate the KV cache. The prompt and the response share this window.
variables.label: Ollama num ctx

variables.description: Most tokens one response may generate, 64-131072. Must not exceed OLLAMA_NUM_CTX.
variables.label: Ollama num predict

variables.description: How hard repeated tokens are discouraged, 0.5-2.0. Above 1.0 penalises repetition.
variables.label: Ollama repeat penalty

variables.description: Thinking-capable models such as qwen3.5 reason before answering unless told not to. With format=json that reasoning can consume the whole turn and leave an empty response, so it is off unless explicitly enabled.
variables.label: Ollama think

variables.description: Google Gemini credential. Setting it is what makes the vendor available; there is no separate provider switch.
variables.label: Gemini api key

variables.description: OpenAI credential. Setting it is what makes the vendor available.
variables.label: Openai api key

variables.description: Anthropic credential. Setting it is what makes the vendor available.
variables.label: Anthropic api key

variables.description: Overall deadline for the entire generation request including all retries and fallbacks. Must be less than ALB idle timeout (120s). Default 110s.
variables.label: AI generation overall timeout seconds

variables.description: Whole-request budget for grading one attempt's open-ended answers, 1-55. It sits below the window a hosted database leaves a transaction idle, so a slow grader costs marks rather than the student's answers.
variables.label: AI grading overall timeout seconds

variables.description: When a generation fails, the logs always describe the model's response by size, digest, top-level key names and the fields validation rejected. Turn this on to add a truncated copy of the response text itself. It is study content, so leave it off unless you are actively diagnosing a failure.
variables.label: AI log raw response on failure

variables.description: Full policy in docs/credits.md. Credits meter hosted AI generation; self-hosted operators supply their own inference, so metering is off for them. Unset, this follows DEPLOYMENT_MODE: true when hosted, false when self_hosted. The value below is spelled out to match this template's DEPLOYMENT_MODE=self_hosted -- change it with the mode, or delete the line to track the mode automatically. While false nothing is charged, refunded, or granted, no charge or refund rows are written, and the API reports a null balance rather than a frozen number.
variables.label: Credit metering enabled

variables.description: Granted once at registration, recorded as an INITIAL_GRANT ledger row.
variables.label: Credit initial grant

variables.description: Granted at most once per calendar month, lazily on the next charge or balance read. The grant is trimmed so it never carries a balance past CREDIT_MAX_BALANCE.
variables.label: Credit periodic grant

variables.description: Ceiling for automatic granting only. It never reduces a balance, and deliberate administrator grants and adjustments are not capped by it.
variables.label: Credit max balance

variables.description: Full policy in docs/rate_limiting.md. Per-IP and per-account login attempts allowed within the window before a 429; the account dimension additionally locks out progressively (see RATE_LIMIT_LOCKOUT_* below).
variables.label: Rate limit login max attempts

variables.description: Window those sign-in attempts are counted over.
variables.label: Rate limit login window seconds

variables.description: Per-IP registration attempts allowed within the window before a 429.
variables.label: Rate limit register max attempts

variables.description: Window those registrations are counted over.
variables.label: Rate limit register window seconds

variables.description: Per-user, per-feature AI generation requests allowed within the window before a 429. Checked ahead of CreditService.charge, so a throttled request never spends credit.
variables.label: Rate limit generation max attempts

variables.description: Window those generation requests are counted over.
variables.label: Rate limit generation window seconds

variables.description: Progressive lockout for repeated account-login violations: the first lockout lasts the base duration, each further violation while still recently locked doubles it, capped at the max.
variables.label: Rate limit lockout base seconds

variables.description: Ceiling on that doubling lockout. Must be at least the base.
variables.label: Rate limit lockout max seconds

variables.description: Per-IP email verification attempts (redeem and resend combined) allowed within the window before a 429. Keyed by IP rather than by address so an attacker cannot lock a victim out of verifying their own account.
variables.label: Rate limit verification max attempts

variables.description: Window those verification sends are counted over.
variables.label: Rate limit verification window seconds

variables.description: Per-IP password reset request attempts allowed within the window before a 429.
variables.label: Rate limit password reset max attempts

variables.description: Window those reset requests are counted over.
variables.label: Rate limit password reset window seconds

variables.description: Authenticated browser crash reports per user in one fixed window.
variables.label: Client error max reports

variables.description: Window those browser error reports are counted over, 1-3600.
variables.label: Client error window seconds

variables.description: Full policy in docs/authentication.md. Minimum password length, enforced identically in registration and password change. Length leads the policy and no character composition is demanded. NIST SP 800-63B floor is 8; bcrypt truncates at 72 bytes, so values above 64 are rejected at startup.
variables.label: Password min length

variables.description: Whether an address must be proven reachable before the account receives its introductory and monthly credits. Unset, this follows DEPLOYMENT_MODE: true when hosted, false when self_hosted. Turning it on requires APP_PUBLIC_BASE_URL, EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS, and SMTP_HOST, because a deployment that cannot deliver the link would create accounts nobody could finish.
variables.label: Email verification required

variables.description: How long an issued verification link stays redeemable. Every link is single-use regardless; this bounds how long a leaked one is worth anything.
variables.label: Email verification token TTL hours

variables.description: How long an issued password reset link stays redeemable.
variables.label: Password reset token TTL minutes

variables.description: Access token (JWT) lifespan. After expiration, a new login is required.
variables.label: Access token expire minutes

variables.description: Origin the verification link points at, without a trailing path. This is the address a user's browser reaches, which is the SPA rather than the API. Example: https://app.example.com
variables.label: Public base URL

variables.description: Envelope sender for verification mail. Use an address the SMTP relay is authorized to send as, or the relay will reject the message. The hosted deployment sends as info@lumina-study.com; a self-hosted one must use its own.
variables.label: Email from address

variables.description: SMTP relay. SMTP_USERNAME and SMTP_PASSWORD are optional; supply both or neither. SMTP_USE_TLS issues STARTTLS after connecting, which is what port 587 expects; disable it only for a relay on the same private network.
variables.label: SMTP host

variables.description: Port for the SMTP host, 1-65535. 587 is submission with STARTTLS.
variables.label: SMTP port

variables.description: SMTP account name. Username and password are both set or both empty; one without the other is refused at startup.
variables.label: SMTP username

variables.description: SMTP account password. Single-quote it if it contains $.
variables.label: SMTP password

variables.description: Whether STARTTLS is negotiated on the connection. Leave it on unless the relay is on this host.
variables.label: SMTP uses TLS

variables.description: Budget for one SMTP conversation, 1-120. Exceeding it fails the send without failing the request that triggered it.
variables.label: SMTP timeout seconds

variables.description: Applied by the application to every response, including the ones middleware returns before a route runs. Existing values are never overwritten, so a proxy or CDN in front of the API stays authoritative for the headers it already sets. Disable only when a boundary you control sets all of them.
variables.label: Security headers enabled

variables.description: HSTS is a promise the browser remembers for a year, so it defaults on only in hosted mode, where TLS is known to terminate in front of the API. A self-hosted deployment behind a TLS reverse proxy should set it to true; one served over plain HTTP must leave it false or browsers will refuse to reach it.
variables.label: HSTS enabled

variables.description: How long a browser should refuse plain HTTP for this host once it has seen the header. Only set a long value once TLS is permanent.
variables.label: HSTS maximum age

variables.description: Publishes /legal/* pages, the legal footer, AI disclosure notices, and the registration Terms/Privacy acknowledgement. Accepts true/false or yes/no.
variables.label: Legal policies enabled

variables.description: ENABLE_HOSTED_ADS controls the optional privacy-preserving advertising path. Strictly forbidden in self_hosted mode (setting true raises a startup error). In hosted mode, defaults to false (kill-switch ready).
variables.label: Hosted advertising enabled

variables.description: Which ad network serves the slots. Hosted deployments only.
variables.label: Hosted ads provider

variables.description: Publisher identifier handed to that network. Hosted deployments only.
variables.label: Hosted ads publisher ID
